Q.3 A queue data structure when implemented using an array post many shortcomings like false overflow (queue is full even though space is available) or overheads of shifting elements if element is deleted to avoid false overflow. Propose a modified queue data structure in which the front and rear indexes of the array be manipulated for enqueuing (insertion) and dequeuing (deletion) of elements eliminating the overhead of elements shifting altogether.
Write the following enqueue and dequeue functions for the modified queue with overflow and underflow conditions.
a) enQ(int * Q, int size, int info) that add integer info at the rear index of the array Q implemented as a Queue.
b) int deQ(int * Q, int size) which delete the element from the front index and return it.

Q.4 In context of sorting the array of integer elements {1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8} using quick sort; arrange these elements for the following cases individually:
a) If pivot is always taken as the first element, and quick sort algorithm needs maximum swaps.
b) If pivot is always taken as the last element, and quick sort algorithm needs minimum swaps.
c) If pivot is always taken as the mid element, and quick sort algorithm needs minimum swaps.
d) If pivot is always taken as the first element, and quick sort algorithm needs minimum swaps.
